key: And Solomon was building his own house thirteen years, and he finished all his house.
s: After the seven years spent on the Temple, the chapter turns to Solomon’s own palace; Rashi, on 7:1, reads the longer span as told in his praise, quick as he was in the work of the Most High and slow in his own.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 1 Kings 7:1 and at [293,1] match. Plain sense faithful: 6:38 closes seven years on the Temple and 7:1 opens the account of Solomon’s own house; no four-word run from the key. Read Rashi across chapter 7 and every packet source on 7:1. Rashi’s own words say he hurried in the work of the Most High, was slow in his own, and that the text tells it in his praise; the sentence paraphrases exactly that (the longer span is the thirteen against the seven years named in the clause). Metzudat David makes the same point; Radak’s note is chronological only, so no disagreement to name.
